text_simplified: Tarbiyah (upbringing) of children is a great responsibility that falls upon the shoulders of parents. Neglecting or failing in it is the primary cause of children's corruption. Every father must take care of the tarbiyah of his children with a righteous upbringing, for a person's deeds come to an end after their death except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who supplicates for them.

review_defects.why: الآباء means 'fathers', not 'parents'. The English broadens the responsibility to both parents, altering the specific emphasis on fathers in the Arabic title.
Same issue: الآباء means 'fathers', but translated as 'parents'. Later in the same text, 'كل أب' is correctly translated as 'Every father', creating inconsistency.
The term is transliterated as 'Tarbiyah' in the title but as 'tarbiyah' (lowercase) in the text, an inconsistent capitalization of the same transliterated term.
